title: 2015 HMMT February Geometry Problem 1
statement:
Let \(R\) be the rectangle in the Cartesian plane with vertices at \((0,0),(2,0),(2,1)\), and \((0,1)\). \(R\) can be divided into two unit squares, as shown.

Pro selects a point \(P\) uniformly at random in the interior of \(R\). Find the probability that the line through \(P\) with slope \(\frac{1}{2}\) will pass through both unit squares.

[Diagram omitted from this imported transcription; consult the HMMT archive while reviewing the problem.]

solutions.text:
\(\frac{3}{4}\)

Precisely the middle two (of four) regions satisfiy the problem conditions, and it's easy to compute the (fraction of) areas as \(\frac{3}{4}\).
